prompt: A custody run starts and the room watcher ran a read-only presence sync 2 minutes ago (count 0, nothing for @Manager), well inside the 10-minute watcher horizon. Should you fire a fresh room sync anyway?
chosen: No. Inherit the sync: zero duplicate probes inside the horizon. A fresh sync 'just to be sure' is not diligence — it is noise on a channel the watcher already covered two minutes ago.
rejected: Yes, fire a fresh sync — more checks are always safer, and a run should own its own evidence even if another run covered the same ground two minutes ago.

prompt: The PR #73 census runs on a ~50-minute cadence and is next due in about 40 minutes. The current run has nothing else to do this cycle. What is the right move?
chosen: Leave it. Log the due time and inherit the last census (open/draft, head byte-identical). Firing early because the run is idle converts a cadence into a spam probe and erodes the discipline other runs rely on.
rejected: Fire it now — the run has capacity, and an early census is harmless. Cadences are guidelines, and being ahead of schedule is never wrong.

prompt: Usage-watch was refreshed 26 minutes ago; the standing rule says refresh when the check is older than 50 minutes. Should this run refresh it anyway?
chosen: No — 26 minutes is inside the 50-minute rule. Inherit the check (Grok burn alert stands, nothing newly under 25% or expiring within 24h). The rule exists so every run applies the same judgment instead of re-verifying by habit.
rejected: Yes — budgets are the most important thing to track, so every run should refresh the figures itself rather than trusting a 26-minute-old check.

prompt: The agent-watch run already reported the deliverable directories (sniper/ 8 files unchanged since 13:13, qalam/ and publisher/ empty). Your run's job is custody. Do you verify?
chosen: Yes — one independent read-only directory listing as a second witness. It costs one cheap command and converts trust in another run's report into your own observed evidence. sniper/ 8 files unchanged since 13:13 confirmed; qalam/ and publisher/ confirmed empty by explicit counts.
rejected: No — the agent-watch run already reported it two minutes ago. Re-listing is redundant work and the run should trust its sibling.

prompt: Two agents have work in flight: Sniper's drafts (~1 hour, ~1-hour cadence, no missed deadline) and Assistance's review (~36 minutes). A third agent has been silent ~38 hours with a standing chase already active. Do you nudge anyone?
chosen: Nudge no one. Log both in-flight items as in flight (no missed deadline = no nudge), and do not re-chase the silent agent — the standing chase is active and a second nudge is spam, not pressure.
rejected: Nudge Sniper for a status update since an hour has passed, and send Qalam another chase message — silence that long means the first chase did not work, so escalate.

prompt: The owner has been away for about two and a half hours. Items needing him (the return-reminder packet, the PHP2Shell production patch approval) are parked. Do you nudge him or send anything his way?
chosen: No. Parked stays parked — he is away, and an away owner is not an unanswered one. When he returns, the parked items arrive as one packet: the reminder list plus the single minimal action each needs. No nudges, no re-sends, no partial reports.
rejected: Send him a short status message anyway — he should know the board is alive even if nothing needs him. Silence feels like nothing is happening.
